newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stocks hit 1997 low in dismal trade.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stocks hit 1997 low in dismal trade.

text.p: Jordanian shares fell in minimal trade on Saturday to their lowest level this year, depressed by political tension in the Middle East and a lack of international buyers over the Western weekend.
The official Amman Financial Market (AFM) index fell 0.12 percent to 151.46 points, its lowest level since December. Turnover of just 122,000 dinars ($172,000) was the lowest in more than a year.
"The market is weak across the board," said one broker. "Everyone is pessimistic today."
Only two companines, Jordan Industrial Resources and Arab International for Investment and Education traded more than 10,000 dinars worth of shares. Both stocks fell.
"Local investors are just waiting," said another broker. "They are holding back because of the Palestinian problems."
The market was waiting to see if foreign funds would revive the market on Monday or whether they would also steer clear of business, he added.
Overall 18 shares fell on Saturday and 10 rose. Another eight were traded but closed unchanged.
